_comment: Feature fingerprints for hd-build-deploy.ps1's anti-clobber check.
Each entry is a string that is present in the built artifact IF AND ONLY IF that
feature's source is in the build. The deploy script reads the CURRENTLY DEPLOYED
artifact, records which markers it contains, and REFUSES to deploy a new build
that has lost any of them - which is exactly the failure that wasted a play-test
on 2026-07-31 (one session rebuilt the shared workspace from sources lacking
another session's portrait fix, and silently deployed a DLL without it).
ADD YOUR OWN MARKER when you add a feature. Pick a literal string your code emits
(a logger format string is ideal - they are unique and survive into the binary).
Cost of a missing marker: your feature is not protected. Cost of a wrong marker:
every deploy is refused until you fix it. Markers absent from the live artifact
are simply not enforced, so a stale entry here is harmless.
PICK A STRING FROM CODE THAT IS ACTUALLY REACHED. A literal inside a function nothing
calls is stripped by the linker, so the marker is silently absent from the binary and
protects nothing. That is what happened to sharmat-bridge on 2026-07-31: its first
marker lived in Sharmat::SetBaseUrl, which has no caller. The deploy reported success
and the manifest simply never listed the feature.
DLL markers must also be NARROW (ASCII) literals. The check reads the binary as ASCII,
so an L-prefixed wide string is stored as UTF-16 and can never match - which is why
the config_manager.php path in sharmat.cpp would be a useless marker.
